land.text: the Lithuanian lands under German occupation in 1918

predecessors.note: 'The Kingdom of Lithuania was a client-state of the German Empire' (Kingdom of Lithuania page, on the 1918 monarchy). No page opened describes the Russian Empire's earlier hold.

land.text: the whole state in 1940: the 1939 shape with Vilnius

successors.note: The People's Seimas asked on 21 July 1940 to join the Soviet Union; 'In early August, the Supreme Soviet of the USSR accepted'. The Lithuanian SSR dossier starts in July 1940.

capitals.name: Vilnius
capitals.note: The Lithuanian Taryba left Vilnius in January 1919 (Vilnius Region page); that the Taryba sat in Vilnius when it declared independence on 16 February 1918 is the researcher's reading, not on the page.

capitals.name: Kaunas
capitals.note: The move to Kaunas is not on any page opened (the Vilnius Region page gives only that the Taryba left Vilnius in January 1919): the standard reading is a provisional capital, with Vilnius claimed throughout ('Lithuania refused to recognize' the Polish action). A gap-filler should confirm.

rulers.name: Mindaugas II (Wilhelm, 2nd Duke of Urach)
rulers.title: King (elected, never visited the country)
rulers.note: 'the 2nd Duke of Urach was invited to become King Mindaugas II'; 'the monarchy was short-lived and Mindaugas II never visited Lithuania'. The presidents of 1919-1940 are not on the pages opened.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1919 but 'On 16 February 1918, Lithuania was re-established as a democratic state'. The 1919 shape is borrowed for 1918, when the country was under German occupation (the 1918 kingdom was 'a client-state of the German Empire', Kingdom of Lithuania page); unverified: page budget.

60,540 km2: unverified, page budget (no infobox area for the interwar state on the pages opened; the Klaipeda Region is 2,657 km2 and the Vilnius area 6,880 km2). In January 1919 the Taryba left Vilnius and 'the first Polish-Soviet military clashes occurred east of the city'. The shape is the Lithuanian state without Klaipeda and mostly without Vilnius.

60,288 km2: unverified, page budget. The 12 July 1920 Soviet-Lithuanian treaty ceded Vilnius on paper; Lithuania held the city after the Polish army's advance in August and lost it to Zeligowski's mutiny in autumn 1920, so the shape (6 of 14 cells within 30 km of Vilnius) is the western Lithuanian side of the demarcation line. The Klaipeda Region stayed under French administration until January 1923.

62,642 km2: +2,354 km2 on 1923, against the Klaipeda Region's 2,657 km2 ('Total: 2,657 km2'): ratio 0.89. Annexed 19 January 1923, confirmed by the Conference of Ambassadors in 1924 and the Klaipeda Convention of 8 May 1924.
62,205 km2: -437 km2 on 1935, unexplained by the pages opened (probably frontier cells); nothing on the pages between 1924 and the March 1939 cession.

correction.text: the 1939 shape plus Vilnius and its environs, ceded 10 October 1939

keyframe_review.note: 59,889 km2: -2,316 km2 on 1938, the Klaipeda Region ceded on 23 March 1939 (2,657 km2). It lacks what Lithuania gained on 10 October 1939: 'About one-fifth of the region, including Vilnius, was ceded to Lithuania by the Soviet Union on 10 October 1939', about 6,880 km2. Add Vilnius for the year-end state.

correction.text: the corrected 1939 shape, Soviet-occupied from 15 June 1940

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1939 although the state lasted to July 1940 (Soviet ultimatum 14 June, invasion 15 June, People's Seimas request 21 July). Same extent as the corrected 1939 shape (about 66,800 km2).

region.text: the Lithuanian lands under German occupation

ledger.note: 16 February 1918: Lithuania is re-established as a state. 'On 16 February 1918, Lithuania was re-established as a democratic state.' The page names no territory; after the declaration 'the monarchy was re-established' under a Duke of Urach as 'King Mindaugas II', a client of the German Empire.

Autumn 1918: the kingdom gives way to a republic. After Germany's defeat 'the idea of a monarchy was abandoned in favor of a democratic republic'; the page gives only the season (month set to November, the month of the German collapse, as a reading).

January 1919: the Lithuanian Taryba leaves Vilnius as Polish-Soviet clashes begin east of the city ('the Lithuanian Taryba left Vilnius'); the seat moves to Kaunas (the destination is not on the page).

region.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

ledger.note: 1920: Lithuania secures Vilnius from the Bolsheviks. The Soviet-Lithuanian Peace Treaty of 12 July 1920 said disputed areas 'were to be transferred to Lithuania'; 'After the Battle of Warsaw in 1920 ... The Bolsheviks then began transferring the area to Lithuania, and Lithuania secured the city of Vilnius.' The page gives no month for the handover.

region.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

ledger.note: Autumn 1920: Poland takes the Vilnius area. 'the Poles took control' after 'a staged mutiny by Lucjan Zeligowski' (the page does not give the 9 October date); Lithuania 'refused to recognize this action or the border'.

region.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

ledger.note: Autumn 1920: Vilnius passes to Zeligowski's Central Lithuania, a Polish-backed state. The Poles took control 'following Polish military action in autumn 1920'; Poland annexed the area on 24 March 1922.

region.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

ledger.note: 24 March 1922: the dispute is settled in fact. The area 'was annexed by Poland on 24 March 1922 thus finalizing Poland's claims over the territory'; Lithuania never recognised it ('It was not until the Polish ultimatum of 1938 that the two states resolved diplomatic relations').

10 January 1923: the Klaipeda Revolt. The infobox dates the revolt '10-15 January 1923'; the text says 'On 9 January 1923' Lithuania 'occupied the territory during the Klaipeda Revolt'. The territory had been under League of Nations control with a French garrison since 15 February 1920.
19 January 1923: the revolt ends in annexation. 'On 19 January, the territory was annexed by Lithuania.'

19 January 1923: Lithuania annexes the Klaipeda Region (2,657 km2). 'On 19 January, the territory was annexed by Lithuania'; confirmed by the Conference of Ambassadors in 1924 and by the Convention of 8 May 1924.

23 March 1939: Lithuania cedes Klaipeda to Germany. 'after an oral ultimatum had caused a Lithuanian delegation to travel to Berlin', the Treaty of the Cession of the Memel Territory was signed in the early hours of 23 March 1939; 'German forces seized the territory even before the official Lithuanian ratification'.

region.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

ledger.note: 10 October 1939: Lithuania receives Vilnius from the Soviet Union. 'About one-fifth of the region, including Vilnius, was ceded to Lithuania by the Soviet Union on 10 October 1939' (about 6,880 km2 of the region's 32,250 km2); the Invasion of Poland page says Lithuania 'received the city of Vilnius and its environs on 28 October 1939'. The same day, a mutual assistance treaty let the Soviets station 20,000 troops in Lithuania (Baltic occupation page).

region.text: the whole state in 1940: the 1939 shape with Vilnius

ledger.note: 15 June 1940: the Soviet Union invades Lithuania. 'On 14 June 1940 the Soviets issued an ultimatum to Lithuania'; 'On 15 June the USSR invaded Lithuania.' Rigged elections for the 'People's Parliaments' followed on 14-15 July.

region.text: the whole state in 1940: the 1939 shape with Vilnius

ledger.note: 21 July 1940: the occupation becomes annexation. 'The People's Parliaments met on 21 July, each with only one piece of business - a request to join the Soviet Union'; 'In early August, the Supreme Soviet of the USSR accepted all three requests.' The Lithuanian SSR dossier starts in July 1940.

region.text: the whole state in 1940: the 1939 shape with Vilnius

ledger.note: 21 July 1940: Lithuania's People's Seimas asks to join the Soviet Union, ending the Republic of Lithuania; the Supreme Soviet accepted 'in early August' (the Soviet dossier dates the incorporation 3 August).

wars.name: Polish-Lithuanian conflict over the Vilnius Region

zones.text: Vilnius and its environs, about 6,880 km2

wars.outcome: Lithuania held Vilnius briefly in 1920 and lost it to Zeligowski's mutiny in autumn 1920; Poland annexed the Vilnius Region on 24 March 1922; Lithuania did not recognise it.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the Suwalki Agreement (7 October 1920) or the mutiny (9 October 1920); the Vilnius area was ceded back to Lithuania by the Soviet Union on 10 October 1939.

wars.name: Klaipeda Revolt
wars.outcome: Lithuania occupied the territory and annexed it on 19 January 1923; the Conference of Ambassadors confirmed it in 1924 and the Klaipeda Convention of 8 May 1924 settled the autonomy.
wars.note: The infobox dates the revolt 10-15 January 1923; the text says 9 January.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Lithuania
wars.outcome: Ultimatum of 14 June, invasion of 15 June, rigged elections of 14-15 July, request of 21 July and acceptance in early August 1940; no fighting.
wars.note: Zones empty: the state yielded without a campaign, so the ledger records an occupation, not a contest.

certainty.note: The frontiers were not fixed: the Polish and Soviet fronts moved around Vilnius and the Suwalki area, and the Klaipeda Region was under League control.

The Klaipeda Convention of 8 May 1924 and the French-run commission fixed the north-west; the line with Poland was only a de facto demarcation line that Lithuania did not recognise (soft), and the Vilnius line of 1939 follows the Soviet cession.
Occupied by the Soviet Union from 15 June 1940; no boundary changes on the pages.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Lithuania' (1919-1939, Q1656775) is not the Kingdom of Lithuania of the page it links: that article is mostly the medieval kingdom of Mindaugas I (1251-1263) with a short paragraph on the 1918 monarchy (July-November 1918, client of the German Empire). The shapes are interwar Lithuania, so this dossier is the Republic of Lithuania from 16 February 1918 to the Soviet annexation of July-August 1940; the row's Wikipedia field and name should be changed to 'Republic of Lithuania (1918-1940)' (the 1990-2024 Cliopatria row 'Republic of Lithuania' is a different, restored state). Not on the pages opened: the capital moves (Kaunas, and whether Vilnius served as capital from 1939), the heads of state, the election of Wilhelm of Urach in July 1918, the date of the 1920 Suwalki agreement and of Zeligowski's mutiny, the German-occupation years 1915-1918, the Suwalki frontier with Poland, and any interwar area figure. The two pages disagree on the Vilnius handover: 10 October 1939 (Vilnius Region page, the treaty) and 28 October 1939 (Invasion of Poland page, the handover); the ledger uses October with 10 October in the note. Counterparts needing a dossier: central-lithuania (October 1920 - March 1922). Existing dossiers used: memel-territory, lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic, nazi-germany, second-polish-republic. The 1919 shape includes some cells of Poland and Belarus (Suwalki and Grodno borderlands) that no page explains; the 1939 correction adds Vilnius by a 47 km radius (about 6,900 km2) because the page gives the area but no boundary. Six pages are cited (five budget; the Interwar_Lithuania URL redirected to a generic Lithuania history page, which still gave the 16 February 1918 sentence).
